info.title: Humaniq
info.description:
The JSON API of Humaniq, the HR app for Nextcloud: employees and contracts, leave and sick leave, time entries and expenses, payroll and payroll tax returns, recruitment, onboarding and offboarding, surveys and the reports behind them. The records themselves are stored in OpenRegister and read and written through its API; this document covers the endpoints Humaniq adds on top.

Every path is served under `/api/v1/`, the version this document describes. The unversioned `/api/` paths keep working, are deprecated, and name their `/api/v1/` successor in a `Link` header next to a `Deprecation` header. Errors are RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`), and every response carries an `API-Version` header. Paths that implement an external standard keep the formats of that standard and are not described here.

post.summary: `POST /api/documents/generate` -- dispatches on `documentType`. The four letter types resolve the posted `contractId` under the caller's RBAC...
post.description: `POST /api/documents/generate` -- dispatches on `documentType`. The four letter types resolve the posted `contractId` under the caller's RBAC (unknown/unauthorized -> 404, no docudesk call) then trigger a single generation attempt for it (humaniq-docudesk-documents design.md D8). `loonstrook` resolves the posted `payslipId` the identical way via `authorizePayslip()` (payslip-pdf-docudesk design.md D6) -- the employeeId is taken from the resolved payslip, `contractId` stays null. A missing subject param for the requested type -> 400. `jaaropgaaf` resolves the posted `jaaropgaafId` the identical way via `authorizeJaaropgaaf()` and renders that statement's employee and year (payroll-annual-statement-action D1). Needs a signed-in Nextcloud user.

post.description: Resolve the employer cost per hour for one employee. `additions` accepts the caller's own per-hour amounts — Shillinq's ledger-derived overhead and equipment pools. They are merged with the employee's stored additions by the service, which also enforces the rules that make the sum defensible: an addition states a fixed amount OR a percentage of the wage base and never both, a percentage resolves against the wage base rather than a running total, and an overtime addition cannot be stacked on a wage base that already blends overtime. Needs a signed-in Nextcloud user.

get.summary: Return the EFFECTIVE app manifest as JSON (ADR-024 §4)
get.description: Return the EFFECTIVE app manifest as JSON (ADR-024 §4). This used to serve `src/manifest.json`, which is the BASE manifest: 11 pages, before the 33 `src/manifest.d/` fragments and the `src/menu-layout.json` relocations are merged in. The shipping app has 113. The SPA never noticed, because it imports the base at build time and runs `buildManifest()` itself at boot, so the only reader this endpoint ever had was a warm-up curl in ci-seed.sh checking a status code. Anyone who trusted it got a manifest describing an app that does not exist. It now serves `src/manifest.effective.json`, which `tests/verify-manifest-parity.js` emits from that same `buildManifest()` and re-verifies on every CI run, so PHP never re-implements the merge and cannot drift from it. There is deliberately NO fallback to the base manifest. Falling back silently is the exact defect this method is being fixed for: it would restore the wrong answer and report success while doing it. Needs a signed-in Nextcloud user.

get.summary: `GET /api/payroll/dga-status` — the self-service gebruikelijkloon compliance status for the caller's OWN DGA record (single-person-modes design.md...
get.description: `GET /api/payroll/dga-status` — the self-service gebruikelijkloon compliance status for the caller's OWN DGA record (single-person-modes design.md D5). Read-only, stateless, persists nothing: 1. Resolves the caller's own `Employee` via `nextcloudUserId` (the `mijn-hr-self-service` link). No `Employee` found, or the resolved `Employee` is not a DGA (`isDga` not `true`) → 200 `{isDga: false, met: null}`. Both cases collapse to the SAME body so the response never distinguishes "no Employee" from "Employee, not a DGA" (D5.1). It is an answer, not an error: the page probes this endpoint for every visitor, and a 404 would log a failed request each time. 2. REUSES `NlDgaChecks`'s existing `nl-gebruikelijkloon-norm` predicate for the `met` verdict — zero new tax logic; the norm comparison is never reimplemented here. The `grossAnnualSalaryCents`/`jaarnormCents` display figures are derived from the SAME annualisation (`grossMonthlySalary × 12`) and the SAME loaded tables' `gebruikelijkloon().jaarnormCents` the predicate uses — read fresh on every call, no caching, no register write, EVER. Needs a signed-in Nextcloud user.

post.summary: `POST /api/payroll/proforma` — the persist-nothing "Simuleer loonstrook" pro-forma simulation (proforma-payslip design.md D4). The caller's access...
post.description: `POST /api/payroll/proforma` — the persist-nothing "Simuleer loonstrook" pro-forma simulation (proforma-payslip design.md D4). The caller's access to the humaniq payroll register/schema is resolved through ObjectService under ambient RBAC BEFORE any computation (a capability probe, not a row lookup — there is no `runId`); a caller who could not see a real Payslip gets a 404, so unauthorized/unavailable collapse to the same status. Only then is the hypothetical input delegated to `ProformaPayslipService::simulate()`. No object is ever read for its data or written. Request parameters: `gross` (bruto maandsalaris in euro, required, numeric), `table` (loonheffingstabel `wit`/`groen`, default `wit`), `loonheffingskorting` (default true), `dateOfBirth` (ISO-8601, or null for below-AOW), `period` (`YYYY-MM`, default the current month), `parttime` (default 1.0), `bijzonder` (one-off bijzondere beloning in euro, default 0), `aof` (`laag`/`hoog` override) and `whk` (percentage override). A non-string `table`, `dateOfBirth`, `period` or `aof` is a bare 400 before anything else, as the dispatcher answers it. Needs a signed-in Nextcloud user.
